scheme_name: Bilateral Trade Promotion Agreement (BTPA) Export Grants
overview: The Bilateral Trade Promotion Agreement (BTPA) Export Grants scheme is part of India's broader international collaboration efforts under the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, aimed at promoting exports through bilateral trade agreements and cooperation frameworks. The scheme supports Indian exporters, particularly MSMEs, by facilitating market access, reducing trade barriers, and enhancing competitiveness in foreign markets through agreements such as FTAs and CEPAs. It focuses on sectors like textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, agriculture, and services, and includes provisions for market access, investment promotion, skill development, and non-tariff barrier reduction. The scheme operates under bilateral and regional trade agreements signed with countries such as the UK, EU, New Zealand, Oman, and Kenya, with implementation coordinated through the Department of Commerce.
objectives: Promote exports of Indian goods and services through bilateral and regional trade agreements
Provide zero-duty or preferential market access for Indian exports in partner countries
Promote inclusive growth by benefiting MSMEs, women, youth, farmers, and artisans
Enhance market access for labour-intensive sectors such as textiles, leather, footwear, gems & jewellery, marine products, and toys
Facilitate technology transfer, innovation, and skill development through cooperation in sectors like IT, healthcare, engineering, and agriculture
Promote investment flows from partner countries into India, including commitments like USD 20 billion from New Zealand
Strengthen cooperation in services, including IT/ITeS, professional services, education, financial services, and digital trade
Address non-tariff barriers through regulatory cooperation, transparency, and streamlined customs and SPS procedures
eligibility: Indian exporters, including MSMEs, startups, women-led enterprises, farmers, artisans, and innovators, engaged in export-oriented activities in sectors such as textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, agriculture, marine products, gems and jewellery, leather, footwear, toys, sports goods, plastics, furniture, automobiles, and services sectors like IT/ITeS, professional services, education, financial services, tourism, construction, and healthcare, are eligible to benefit from the market access, investment promotion, skill development, and non-tariff barrier reduction provisions under bilateral trade agreements such as FTAs and CEPAs signed by India with partner countries.
benefits: Beneficiaries gain access to zero-duty or preferential market access in partner countries, enhanced market access in labour-intensive and high-value sectors, opportunities for skill development and training under initiatives like ITEC and 'Study in India', access to investment commitments (e.g., USD 20 billion from New Zealand), support for innovation and technology transfer, facilitation of market entry through faster regulatory approvals (e.g., pharma and medical devices via GMP/GCP recognition), promotion of traditional medicine and AYUSH systems globally, support for Geographical Indications (GI) protection, access to Centres of Excellence for agricultural productivity (e.g., apples, kiwifruit, honey), enhanced mobility for professionals through visa commitments (e.g., 5,000 skilled visas to New Zealand), and support for MSMEs through export readiness programmes, trade-related information linkages, and integration into global value chains.
financial_support: Financial support under the BTPA Export Grants scheme is delivered indirectly through bilateral trade agreements that unlock market access and investment opportunities rather than direct cash grants. Key financial mechanisms include investment commitments from partner countries (e.g., New Zealand’s commitment to facilitate USD 20 billion in investment into India), support for setting up Centres of Excellence in agriculture and technology, facilitation of collateral-free loans under initiatives like #GeMSahay, and support for export credit through ECGC schemes such as Collateral-Free Cover for MSEs up to Rs.10 crore and enhanced cover up to Rs.50 crore 50 crore. The scheme also enables access to government procurement platforms like GeM and supports export promotion through Market Access Initiative (MAI) and Interest Equalisation Scheme (IES).
application_process: 1. Identify relevant bilateral trade agreement (FTA/CEPA) under which your sector or product qualifies for benefits. 2. Confirm eligibility based on product/sector coverage under the agreement (e.g., textiles, pharma, engineering goods, agriculture, services). 3. Ensure compliance with rules of origin and product-specific rules under the agreement. 4. Obtain necessary certifications such as GMP/GCP for pharma, GI registration for handicrafts, or organic certification where applicable. 5. Register with relevant Export Promotion Councils (EPCs) or Commodity Boards for sector-specific support. 6. Avail benefits such as zero-duty access by submitting shipping bills and documentation through ICEGATE or DGFT portals. 7. Apply for export promotion schemes like Market Access Initiative (MAI) or Interest Equalisation Scheme (IES) through DGFT for financial support. 8. Utilize platforms like Trade Connect ePlatform and Trade Intelligence & Analytics (TIA) for market intelligence and trade facilitation. 9. Avail skill development or training programmes under ITEC or 'Study in India' for skill enhancement. 10. Engage with Indian missions abroad or Export Promotion Councils for business matchmaking and participation in international exhibitions (e.g., Autoexpo Kenya, The Big 5 Construct Kenya).
required_documents: Shipping Bill / Shipping Bill of Export
GMP/GCP inspection reports (for pharmaceuticals and medical devices)
Export Promotion Council (EPC) / Commodity Board membership certificate
GI application or registration documents (for GI products)
Test reports from recognized laboratories (for quality compliance)
Transport document (Bill of Lading / Airway Bill)
Inspection Certificate (if required by importing country)
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications and benefit claims under bilateral trade agreements are accepted throughout the year as per shipment timelines and scheme-specific windows (e.g., MAI, IES).
implementing_agency: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
contact_details: Email: recruitment-e2@gov.in | Helpline: Not explicitly mentioned in evidence
caveats: Benefits are product- and sector-specific and depend on the terms of individual bilateral trade agreements (FTAs/CEPAs)
Zero-duty access is subject to meeting rules of origin and product-specific criteria under each agreement
Certain sensitive sectors (e.g., dairy, cereals, poultry, soyabean oil, tobacco) are excluded or protected under exclusion or TRQ mechanisms in agreements
Benefits under schemes like MAI and IES are subject to annual budget allocations and scheme-specific guidelines
Export benefits require compliance with documentation and procedural requirements under DGFT and customs regulations
Investment commitments (e.g., USD 20 billion from New Zealand) are facilitative in nature and do not guarantee direct fund disbursement to individual enterprises
Skill development and training programmes (e.g., ITEC, Study in India) have separate eligibility criteria and application processes
Geographical Indication (GI) benefits require separate registration and legal protection processes
Benefits under CEPAs/FTAs are subject to ratification and entry into force of the respective agreements
Benefits may be subject to rebalancing or review clauses if investment or market access commitments are not met by partner countries
